title: Convert Sorted Array to Binary Search Tree
description:
Given an integer array nums where the elements are sorted in ascending order, convert it to a height-balanced binary search tree.

Build the tree recursively: choose the middle element of each subarray as its root; when the subarray has even length, choose the left middle element. Apply the same rule to the left and right subarrays. Return that exact tree in level order, with nulls marking missing children (omit trailing nulls).

A height-balanced binary tree is a binary tree in which the depth of the two subtrees of every node never differs by more than one.

Example 1:

Input: nums = [-10,-3,0,5,9]
Output: [0,-10,5,null,-3,null,9]
Explanation: The prescribed middle-element construction gives this tree.

Example 2:

Input: nums = [1,3]
Output: [1,null,3]
Explanation: For two elements, choose the left middle (1) as the root.

Constraints:

  • 1 ≤ nums.length ≤ 10^4
  • -10^4 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 10^4
  • nums is sorted in a strictly increasing order
